newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Gerard sees room for lower rates in Europe.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Gerard sees room for lower rates in Europe.

text.p: There is room for lower short term interest rates in Europe, Jean-Pierre Gerard, member of the Bank of France's monetary policy committee said in a newspaper interview to be published on Thursday.

"I think that today there is room to manoeuvre for lower short term interest rates. But this room to manoeuvre within two years of the euro (European single currency) must be used in the framework of a common policy, and in agreement with Germany and all the countries of Europe," Gerard said in an interview with financial daily l'Agefi.
He said Germany, the Netherlands and some other European countries were maintaining overly restrictive monetary policies.

He added that while some past monetary policy decisions in France led its European partners to regard its actions with suspicion, those partners were stuck in old-fashioned monetary management styles.

"It is true that certain of our actions in the past were viewed with suspicion by our partners. It is no less true that they still rely on their old behaviour, and their old successes, while the room for manoeuvre exists and together we are not taking advantage of it."
He said France had some room to cut rates independently of Germany, but questioned whether the slight cuts that were possible would be worth the risk of roiling financial markets.

"Certainly France by itself has a little room to manoeuvre, but to use it alone would put us at risk," he said. "It is not worth running the risk in the markets for something that has very limited economic efficiency."
The Bank of France's intervention rate is at 3.10 percent, 10 basis points above the German repo rate, commonly viewed as its equivalent.
